pr_title: session, chunk: refactor re-used chunk allocator in executor
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #49661

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?

I considered three features:

1. The allocator in the `BaseExecutor` should be able to allocate concurrently.
2. The session variable `tidb_enable_reuse_chunk` should be able to set whether to reuse chunks between statements.
3. The session variable `last_sql_use_alloc` should tell the user whether the last query used the cached chunk.

issue_context.title: re-organize the reuse chunk pool implementation
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

Sometimes, we re-used the chunk pool to avoid re-allocating memories across multiple statements. This chunk pool located in the "connection", and is set into session context when it's possible to re-use the allocator. This part of code is quite confusing:

1. `chunk.Allocator` is not safe to call concurrently. Therefore, we always use `GetNewChunkWithCapacity` to allocate chunks from the allocator, and it'll use `(*SessionVars).ChunkPool.mu` to protect the allocator inside the `BaseExecutor`. It's reasonable because usually all `BaseExecutor` just used the `ChunkPool` in session context. However, just from the code, the relationship between the `(*SessionVars).ChunkPool.mu` and the `BaseExecutor.Alloc` is not significant.
2. We expect to remove session context from the `BaseExecutor`, so we have to remove the `GetNewChunkWithCapacity` function call in the implementation of `BaseExecutor`.

And also, we'll need to use a session variable to tell whether the re-use chunk pool optimization is enabled. Also, we have a read-only session variable to tell the users whether last statement used the re-used chunk :facepalm: . It's a little complicated.
comments: BR/lightning has a []byte pool https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/br/pkg/membuf/buffer.go , do you think our usage are similar so we can unify them?

> BR/lightning has a []byte pool https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/br/pkg/membuf/buffer.go , do you think our usage are similar so we can unify them?

For this issue, I'm not going to rewrite `chunk.(*allocator)`, but only refactor `variable.ReuseChunkPool`, which is used to re-use the same `(*allocator)` in a session across many different queries.

review_comments: Is it safe to remove lock here？

The usage of `.chunkPool` field is quite limited. After analyzing the codes, I think it's fine.

I've also discussed with @keeplearning20221 (who is the original author of the re-used chunk). He also agrees it's safe to do so.

By the way, the use of `MaxChunkSize` is not reasonable, we met Go GC issues when the column length is varchar(1500)/varchar(3000)... in that case the chunk object size amplify too much and cause high pressue on Go GC.
We can take a close look of all `sessVars.MaxChunkSize` chunk allocating later.

Do you think it would be better to also use `BaseExecutor.InitCap` and `BaseExecutor.MaxChunkSize` here? Though the current context doesn't have this information, we can pass them (to the `hashJoinCtx`).
I haven't check the code for how `MaxChunkSize` is used yet, so no suggestions.

Can we retun something like a `DefaultEmptyAllocator` instead?  (see also `context.Background()`)
Creating a `&emptyAllocator{}` is unnecessary and it increase object allocating
